subject: How the portable conventions reach a session
note: A dated reading of the delivery topology, not a registry and not a derived artifact. Every snapshot is what one container held on its date: the pinned-install count varies by machine and the session checkout's branch varies by session, so no commit hook can restamp this and no test can hold it. Same standing as docs/injection.json, which measures the bytes this measures the routes for. A snapshot with state 'planned' is a design, not a measurement.

routes.note: fetched both documents whole, 36,135 bytes, and passed the harness limit on 2026-08-07. From that day the session received the first 2,000 bytes and SURFACING.md did not arrive at all, for nineteen days, while the hook reported success.

evidence: A SessionStart hook over the limit exits 0 and reports success, so the failure was invisible from inside the script.
The fix has to be a payload sized to the channel plus a script that says when it could not fit.

Rung 2 exists because 127 bytes over the budget cost every surfacing primitive.

caps.label: harness ceiling
caps.caveat: keeps the first ~2,000 bytes and discards the rest, silently

evidence: 12 of the 47 recorded sessions carrying both an @-import and an injection receipt for SURFACING.md had the two routes deliver different versions.
The version the injector kept delivering, sha dc188a49, is SURFACING.md as of 2026-08-27. It was still arriving on 2026-09-01.
This session's payload came to 28,026 bytes against the 28,000 ceiling and was cut. The 1,210-byte gap between the pinned copy and the tip is larger than the 26-byte overrun.

stores.upkeep: frozen: it is whatever the pin held when it was taken
stores.note: Fallback only, and only real if the deletion ships one release AFTER the resolver. A plugin install is one tree at one commit, so a pin carrying the new script also carries the deletion, and a pin carrying the copies also carries the old script. Shipped together, this rung can never fire.

caps.label: injector budget
caps.caveat: drops a rung and prints what it withheld

caps.label: harness ceiling
caps.caveat: keeps the first ~2,000 bytes and discards the rest, silently

evidence: Deleting the vendored copy removes three of the six: the copy on main, the clone's copy of it, and the copy inside every pin.
The pinned script still lags by a session. What stops lagging is the document it reads, which is the thing that governs the session.
New risk, not present today: an old pinned script reading new-tip documents is a pair CI never tests, because injected-docs.test.mjs gates the two at one commit.
